title: Path of Exile 2's Shadow turns every fight into an ambush

blocks.text: BANGKOK, Thailand — Stealth classes are hardly new to RPGs, but Path of Exile 2’s Shadow isn’t trying to be another rogue that simply disappears, lands a backstab, and repeats the process.

blocks.caption: The Shadow, one of the new classes arriving with Path of Exile 2’s full release, specializes in stealth, traps, and assassination. Image by Grinding Gear Games

blocks.text: Instead, Grinding Gear Games is building an assassin whose entire gameplay loop revolves around preparation, execution, and momentum.

During the Path of Exile 2 World Tour stop in Bangkok, we got to go hands-on with the Shadow ahead of the game’s Dec. 11 full release and speak with game director Jonathan Rogers about the thinking behind the class.
What stood out immediately wasn’t its damage output or flashy abilities, but how differently it approaches combat compared to a typical action RPG character.
“The key thing for me was to get across the feeling of the ambush,” Rogers told TechINQ.
Making stealth matter

The Shadow is one of the headline additions coming with Path of Exile 2’s full release, specializing in stealth, daggers, traps, and assassination. But while invisibility is central to the class, Rogers said the team’s goal was never simply to give players another way to avoid enemies.
Instead, the class was designed around creating opportunities before a fight even begins.

According to Rogers, one of the earliest breakthroughs came from rethinking how traps interact with stealth. Unlike traditional trap skills that are thrown directly into combat, the Shadow allows players to prepare traps while concealed, effectively turning encounters into planned ambushes.
“In Path of Exile 1, we had traps, but they just kind of didn’t really feel like you were ambushing anything,” Rogers said. “You just kind of throw them at monsters and they go off.”
That changed once the team introduced the ability to preload traps while hidden.

“The thing where stealth doesn’t detonate them, and then you can kind of preload them and attack them. As soon as we had that, that was the moment that I felt that we’d found the fun gameplay of the class,” Rogers explained.

Traps placed while a player is in stealth remain inactive until the player reveals themselves, allowing multiple effects to be layered before an encounter begins. That emphasis on planning extends beyond traps and into the Shadow’s core combat loop.

blocks.caption: The Shadow uses stealth and rapid repositioning to chain attacks together while staying one step ahead of enemies. Image by Grinding Gear Games

blocks.text: A class built on momentum
Stealth is not simply an opening tool for the Shadow. It serves as the foundation for the class’s overall combat rhythm.
A successful kill immediately refreshes stealth, allowing players to disappear again and quickly chain encounters together.
“If you kill someone, you can immediately go into stealth again,” Rogers said.
That flow made the Shadow feel noticeably faster than many traditional ARPG archetypes, but the mechanic comes with an important tradeoff.
“It’s designed to go from pack to pack really fast,” Rogers said. “The tricky thing for a player, and this is actually what I find quite fun about it, is it’s easy for it to go wrong.”

A failed ambush, an overlooked monster, or an enemy that survives longer than expected can immediately break that momentum. Without a kill, players must wait for the stealth cooldown before attempting the sequence again.
That risk-reward balance may ultimately be what makes the Shadow stand out among Path of Exile 2’s roster.
“It’s a class where if everything’s going to plan, then you’re incredibly powerful,” he said. “But when things don’t go to plan, suddenly you’re like, ‘Oh, I need to suddenly rethink what I’m doing.”

Inspired by decades of stealth games
Despite the Shadow’s distinct identity, Rogers said there was no single inspiration behind the class.
Instead, it emerged from years of playing stealth-focused games and understanding the expectations players already bring to assassin-style characters.

“I don’t know if I can pick a specific inspiration, because it’s kind of like every stealth game,” Rogers said. “I’ve played so many different ones that do that. It really is a mix of all the ideas that come from that.”
The class itself has been in development for years.

According to Rogers, many of Path of Exile 2’s characters, including the Shadow, were planned early in development, with their personalities, visual identities, and voice actors established long before players would eventually see them in action.

blocks.caption: Traps, poison effects, and explosive skill combinations form the core of the Shadow’s ambush-focused playstyle. Image by Grinding Gear Games

blocks.text: More than another assassin

Beyond stealth and traps, the Shadow introduces additional systems including Darkness, a new resource that empowers attacks from stealth, Shades that can replicate attacks and deceive enemies, and Eclipse, an ability that temporarily transforms attacks into stealth strikes. Players will also be able to choose between two Ascendancies, Assassin and Infiltrator.
Yet after spending time with the class in Bangkok, none of those systems felt as important as the central idea tying everything together: turning every encounter into a carefully planned ambush.
For Rogers, that uniqueness remains the guiding principle behind every class in Path of Exile 2.

“The main thing for us is that every class has to have something unique about it that the other classes don’t do,” he said. “Can I give someone a unique experience so that each class they play, they feel like having a different experience than what they had from the previous one?”

Based on early hands-on experience, the Shadow is already succeeding on that front. Whether sneaking through encounters, chaining stealth resets, or setting up elaborate trap combinations before enemies even know they’re there, the Shadow is shaping up to be one of the most distinctive additions arriving with Path of Exile 2’s full release on Dec. 11.
